(At Present Lodged In District Jail, Bhilwara)
 ----Petitioner  Versus 1. The State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Mst. Pooja Vaishnav D/o Dinesh Vaishnav, R/o Paldi,
 Police Station Sadar, Dist. Bhilwara.

----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Rajendra Charan For Respondent(s) : Mr. S.S. Rajpurohit, P.P.
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 19/10/2023

This second application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.211/2021 registered at Police Station Sadar Bhilwara, District Bhilwara for the offence under Section 376(2)(N) IPC.
The first bail application of the petitioner was dismissed as not pressed by this Court vide order dated 03.05.2023.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the statements of the prosecutrix have been recorded before competent criminal court as P.W.-1.

Learned counsel submitted that the prosecutrix in her Court's statements has admitted a number of Whatsapp chats and photographs had been shared and [2023:RJ-JD:36141] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-12269/2023] exchanged by the prosecutrix with the petitioner.

Learned counsel submitted that the admission of Whatsapp chats and photographs being exchanged is prima facie indicative of the fact that the prosecutrix had developed consensual physical relationship with the present petitioner out of her free will and volition.

However, on their Himanshu Harivyasi vs The State Of Rajasthan ... on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10491728/
1 relations turning strained, the prosecutrix has falsely roped the petitioner in a criminal case.

sentences.text: Lastly, it was submitted that the statements of the prosecutrix have also been recorded and there are no chances of she being influenced by the present petitioner; the petitioner is in judicial custody since 21.01.2023 and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time.
On these grounds, he implored the court to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, so also the fact that the prosecutrix during her Court's statements has admitted that a number of Whatsapp chats,
messages and photographs were exchanged by her with the present petitioner, the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner that the prosecutrix was in consensual relationship with the petitioner cannot be brushed aside at this stage.

This Court prima facie finds that the statements of the prosecutrix have been recorded before competent criminal court [2023:RJ-JD:36141] (3 of 3)
[CRLMB-12269/2023] and there are no chances of she being influenced by the present petitioner,
without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Consequently, the second bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner - Himanshu Harivyasi S/o Mahaveer Prasad arrested in connection with F.I.R.
No.211/2021 registered at Police Station Sadar Bhilwara, District Bhilwara shall be released on bail,
if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 18-Ravi Khandelwal Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
